mathdial.compared: every reply, plus learner messages of at least 6 words; shorter messages such as bare numbers or acknowledgements are expected to coincide and are skipped

deduplication.method: exact reply match; normalized match after casefolding, masking numbers and stripping punctuation; near-duplicate when word 3-gram Jaccard is at least 0.85; earlier example_id wins

generating_model.name: Claude Fable 5.1
generating_model.runtime: Claude Code agent acting for Person A

license.name: original
license.note: authored for this project; no external source

lineage: Loaded authored records and the frozen split manifest.
Sampled each item with B's family sampler and solved it with B's solver.
Built each TeachingPlan with B's plan builder and applied the listed normalizations.
Graded every learner answer with B's grader and error generators against the item the dialogue last showed.
Validated plans against learning_v1, plan rules and B's response stub.
Ran the six response checks, solver agreement and phrase disclosure on every reply.
Validated every example against the SFTExample schema.
Removed exact, normalized and near-duplicate replies, and MathDial matches.
notes: All examples are model-written and pending human review; checks are automated.
Examples live in data/sft (ignored); the authored records are the committed source.
plan_modifications: concept_name and goal_name use the catalogue names instead of concept IDs
forbidden_answer_fingerprints holds the solver answer when reveal is forbidden
response_context carries the authored dialogue and learner message
PROBE and CHECK_MASTERY items come from teaching families, never assessment ones
REFLECT previous_step is a learner-facing description of the earlier step
split_rule: Every example inherits the split of its template family, the one Person B assigned in packages/learning/content/templates/families.py (SPLIT_BY_VARIANT): teach_01 and teach_02 train, teach_03 validation, teach_04 test. original_problem_id is '<family>:seed<sampler seed>', so every parameter variant stays with its family. Examples whose plan carries no item are anchored to the family of the learner's active item, or for session-level examples to the first teaching family of the split, as B's plan builder does for worked examples.
